message.content:
Below is a quick “starter kit” for pulling all comments that belong to **apple.com** using your `delta_key`.  
Pick the snippet that matches the tool/language you’re comfortable with (or just copy‑paste it into a terminal).

---

## 1️⃣  Raw HTTP (cURL)

```bash
# Replace <YOUR_DELTA_KEY> with the key you received from Delta
curl -s \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_DELTA_KEY>" \
     "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments" \
| jq   # optional: pipe to jq for pretty‑printing
```

*If you prefer to send the key as a query string instead of a header:*

```bash
curl -s \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?delta_key=<YOUR_DELTA_KEY>" \
| jq
```

> **Tip:**  
> *`jq`* is a lightweight JSON processor that makes the output easier to read.  
> If you don’t have it installed, just remove the `| jq` part and you’ll see raw JSON.

---

## 2️⃣  Python (requests)

```python
import requests

API_URL = "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments"
HEADERS = {
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Authorization": f"Bearer <YOUR_DELTA_KEY>"
}

resp = requests.get(API_URL, headers=HEADERS)
resp.raise_for_status()          # will raise an exception if the request failed
comments = resp.json()           # parsed JSON payload

print(comments)                  # or process it however you like
```

> **Note:**  
> If you’re working in a Jupyter notebook or a REPL, you can install `requests` via `pip install requests`.

---

## 3️⃣  Delta SDK (Python)

Delta ships a small SDK that wraps the HTTP calls for you.  

```bash
pip install delta-sdk   # or pip install delta
```

```python
from delta import Client

client = Client(api_key="<YOUR_DELTA_KEY>")
comments = client.get_comments(domain="apple.com")

print(comments)
```

> **Why use the SDK?**  
> It handles pagination automatically, so you’ll get *all* comments without having to manually loop over pages.

---

## 4️⃣  Handling Pagination (if you’re using raw HTTP)

The `/domains/{domain}/comments` endpoint returns results in pages (default 50 per page).  
Add the `page` and `per_page` query parameters to navigate:

```bash
# Page 1
curl -s "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?page=1&per_page=100&delta_key=<YOUR_DELTA_KEY>"

# Page 2
curl -s "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?page=2&per_page=100&delta_key=<YOUR_DELTA_KEY>"
```

> **Tip:**  
> Most SDKs expose a `list()` method that yields items across all pages automatically.

---

## 5️⃣  Quick sanity check

If you want to confirm that your key works before pulling all comments, try a lightweight “health” endpoint:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_DELTA_KEY>" \
     "https://api.delta.com/v1/health" | jq
```

A successful response looks like:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "message": "Your key is valid."
}
```

---

### Recap

| Step | What to do | Why |
|------|------------|-----|
| 1 | Pick a method (cURL, requests, SDK) | Choose what fits your workflow |
| 2 | Replace `<YOUR_DELTA_KEY>` with your real key | Authenticates you |
| 3 | Call `/v1/domains/apple.com/comments` | Retrieves comments for apple.com |
| 4 | Handle pagination if needed | Get *all* comments |

That’s it! Once you run one of those snippets, you’ll receive a JSON array of comment objects that you can parse, store, or analyze further. Happy coding!
